name: How Long Does a San Diego Kitchen Renovation Take From Design to Final Inspection?

mainEntity.name: How long should I plan to be without a working kitchen during a remodel in San Diego?
mainEntity.text: How long should I plan to be without a working kitchen during a remodel in San Diego?

acceptedAnswer.text: Plan for two schedules: the total project period and the time the kitchen cannot function normally. Design, selections, ordering, permit review, demolition, construction, countertop fabrication, inspections, and punch-list work all affect the full timeline. The working-kitchen outage is usually shorter than the entire project, but it can still last several weeks. Before demolition, create a temporary food area with a refrigerator, microwave, induction burner, sink access, storage, and safe outlets. Ask whether the contractor will maintain a temporary water supply and how dust will be contained. Clarify the exact dates for demolition, rough inspections, cabinet installation, countertop templating, appliance delivery, final connections, and final inspection. Order long-lead items early and do not schedule demolition until cabinets, appliances, fixtures, and critical hardware are confirmed. A written schedule should identify owner decisions, contractor responsibilities, inspection dependencies, and allowances for delayed materials. Reviews of local projects frequently mention unclear completion estimates and communication problems, so require weekly updates and written notice of any schedule change.
acceptedAnswer.description: A full San Diego kitchen renovation often takes several months from design through final inspection, while the active construction period may last roughly four to eight weeks after materials arrive. Cabinet lead times, permit review, countertop templating, inspections, and change orders can extend the schedule. Ask for separate design, procurement, construction, and closeout dates.
